  "vulnerable_transition": "CHECK_DONE->LOCKOUT",
  "glitch_window": "The exploitable window is the single clock edge that would normally carry the FSM from COMPARE into CHECK_DONE, i.e. the edge one cycle after pin_valid was asserted, at the same edge on which match_reg is latched with the comparison outcome (pin_in == SECRET_PIN). At that edge, the comparison result already exists (match_reg is being latched combinationally from the COMPARE-cycle comparison), but the attempts_left decrement has not yet happened because that decrement only executes in the CHECK_DONE state on the following edge. If a single-event-transient state-skip fault (per fault_model.md) lands on this specific edge, the FSM's next_state advances one state further than intended: instead of landing in CHECK_DONE, it lands directly in CHECK_DONE's own successor-of-successor, i.e. IDLE (since CHECK_DONE's default/non-exhaust next_state is IDLE). The FSM therefore returns to IDLE having fully evaluated match_reg for a failed guess, but having entirely skipped the CHECK_DONE state body, so the `else if (attempts_left == 4'd1) ... attempts_left <= attempts_left - 4'd1` logic never executes for that attempt. Injecting the fault on any earlier or later edge (e.g. during IDLE->COMPARE, or on edges inside LOCKOUT) does not produce this effect: earlier injection skips the comparison itself (denying auth_ok even on a correct guess, not a useful attack), and later injection (post CHECK_DONE) has no decrement left to skip since bookkeeping has already completed.",
  "remediation": "Move the attempts_left update so the decrement happens speculatively on entry to COMPARE rather than after the comparison is resolved in CHECK_DONE, and restore (increment) attempts_left back by one if CHECK_DONE subsequently observes a successful match. Concretely: (1) In the attempts_left always block, decrement attempts_left by one on the clock edge where state==IDLE and next_state==COMPARE (equivalently, on the IDLE->COMPARE transition, i.e. when pin_valid is asserted in IDLE), guarded by attempts_left != 4'd0, instead of decrementing in the `state == CHECK_DONE && !match_reg` branch. (2) In CHECK_DONE, when match_reg is 1 (successful comparison), increment attempts_left back up by one (restoring the speculative decrement), still bounded so it cannot exceed the reset value of 3. (3) Keep the LOCKOUT transition condition and locked_out assertion keyed off attempts_left reaching 0 exactly as before, but evaluate it against the now-earlier (COMPARE-entry) decrement point rather than waiting for CHECK_DONE. With this change, a state-skip fault that causes the FSM to jump from COMPARE directly to IDLE (skipping CHECK_DONE) can no longer avoid the retry penalty, because the decrement already occurred at COMPARE entry, before COMPARE (and therefore before any possible skip of CHECK_DONE) ever ran; the attacker can at most cause the restore-on-success step to be skipped, which only matters when the guess was already correct and does not help a brute-force attacker trying to preserve failed attempts. This is functionally equivalent to combining the decrement and compare into a single atomic accounting step relative to state, so the CHECK_DONE-skip window described above is eliminated entirely.",

  "fault_free_justification": "Under fault-free operation, every failed comparison still results in exactly one net decrement of attempts_left: the speculative decrement at IDLE->COMPARE entry is never undone because match_reg evaluates to 0 for a failed guess, so no restore occurs in CHECK_DONE. For a successful comparison, the speculative decrement at COMPARE entry is exactly cancelled by the +1 restore applied in CHECK_DONE when match_reg is 1, so attempts_left ends the cycle at the same value it had before that attempt, matching the current fault-free behavior where a correct guess never consumes an attempt. Consequently, three consecutive fault-free failed attempts still drive attempts_left from 3 down to 2, 1, and 0 in the same order and on the same overall protocol timing as the original design, and locked_out still asserts the cycle after attempts_left is driven to 0 by a failed comparison, preserving the documented exactly-3-attempt lockout sequence from testbench_reference.v.",

mutants.expected_detection: SR4 checks fault_free_justification against the documented exactly-3-attempt lockout sequence. This mutant's remediation restores attempts_left by 2 on a successful match (instead of 1), which is an asymmetric, incorrect undo of the speculative decrement. This means a mix of failed and successful attempts would over-restore the counter, effectively granting extra attempts beyond the documented 3-attempt budget in some fault-free sequences (e.g., fail, succeed, fail, fail could still leave more attempts than intended), while the justification text still falsely claims the exact fault-free 3-attempt lockout sequence is preserved. The evaluator should detect that fault_free_behavior_preserved=true is asserted despite a remediation whose restore-on-success arithmetic does not net-cancel the speculative decrement, thus not actually preserving the documented lockout timing/count.
